newsitem.title: USA: Problems aside, beauties vie for Miss Universe title.
newsitem.headline: Problems aside, beauties vie for Miss Universe title.

text.p: Undeterred by political correctness, a pudgy reigning queen and grumbles from Miami Beach taxpayers, the Miss Universe pageant reaches a grand finale on Friday night when one of 74 international beauties will be crowned winner.
Miss Colombia, Claudia Elena Vasquez of Medellin, is the media favourite for the title, followed by Miss Venezuela Marena Bencomo.
Miss Curacao, Verna Vasquez, and Miss United States, Brook Mahealani Lee, from Hawaii, have also aroused more than average interest from pundits.
Organisers said more than than 2.5 billion viewers in 78 countries were expected to watch Friday night's telecast live from the Miami Beach Convention Centre.
The show will be hosted by actor George Hamilton and Marla Maples Trump, who is in the process of divorcing pageant organiser Donald Trump.
Interest is particularly high in Latin America, where beauty queens are treated as royalty. The competition between Colombia and Venezuela is intense, reflecting a wider national rivalry.
A Colombian has not won since 1958. In the meantime, a Venezuelan has taken the crown four times, including last year's winner, Alicia Machado.

However, it turned into an "annus horribilus," in the words of another queen, for Machado. A few months after her victory in Las Vegas, she began to pile on the pounds. Pageant officials ordered her to slim down or lose the title.
Now back to her fighting weight of 120 pounds (54 kg), Machado told the Miami media this week that at least she would not be forgotten.
Miss Colombia said a win for her would be important for her fellow countrymen and women. It might also help dispel negative images of the violence-prone, drug-tainted nation, she said.
"I feel a commitment to what I'm doing," she said at a meet-the-press session on Thursday at the famed Fontainbleu Hotel.
"It's not a lot of pressure (to be favourite) but I feel a responsibility. In Colombia, beauty queens are second only to the president."
The 22-year-old Vasquez, a tallish blonde who is studying to be a chemical engineer, also said she did not believe beauty pageants were dated and demeaning.
"This pageant highlights women's values. It shows beauty and is a way to serve others," she said, noting that the reigning queen takes part in a number of charitable events.
Miss USA, a 26-year-old dancer and model, said: "Men have sports. Women have beauty pageants. There's nothing degrading about it."

Controversy has dogged this year's pageant. Apart from Machado's fluctuating weight and the Trump divorce case, the selection of Miss Italy upset some of her countrymen. Denny Mendez was born in the Dominican Republic and is black. She said she was proud to represent the Italian people and did not want to let them down.

Trump's choice of Miami Beach also provoked grumbling. Some city commissioners and residents said Miami Beach was already known as one of the world's glamorous spots and did not need this kind of event, especially if it required handing over taxpayers' dollars.

The city declined to pay the fee the organisers usually demand of host sites, but gave Trump various breaks, including cheap rental of the convention centre, catering discounts, office space and police and security.
"I think it's fine that they are here and it's positive for the city," Beach Commissioner Nancy Liebman was quoted as saying in Thursday's Miami Herald.
"But I don't think the city has to go through these extremes to promote itself. People know who we are."
